metric_provenance.source_excerpt_or_description: The paper NEVER states whether the reference image is removed from the candidate gallery. Relevant passages: §3, printed page 5 - 'At inference time, given a query (I_q, T_q), we utilize the fine-tuned CLIP encoders and the trained Combiner network to generate the combined features. Subsequently, following the standard image-to-image retrieval approach, we compute the cosine distances between the combined features and the database of index image features. The results are then sorted based on their similarity.' §4.2.1, printed page 10 - 'We follow the standard experimental setting as in [29, 31]. We employ the average recall at rank K (Recall@K), namely Recall@10 (R@10) and Recall@50 (R@50). Note that for each triplet, there is only a positive index image. Hence, each query has R@K zero or one. All results are on the validation set...' §4.1, printed page 9 - 'During retrieval, we normalize both the combined and index set features to have a unit L2-norm.' No sentence anywhere in the paper uses removal/masking/exclusion language for the reference; `grep -n -i 'gallery\|candidate\|exclud\|database\|index set' /tmp/clip4cir.txt` returns only the passages quoted plus 'database' in the intro.

(2) The internal contrast in the SAME file is the strongest evidence that this is deliberate: the CIRR path DOES remove the reference - `:163-166` reference_mask = torch.tensor(sorted_index_names != np.repeat(np.array(reference_names), len(index_names)).reshape(...)), then `sorted_index_names = sorted_index_names[reference_mask].reshape(..., shape[1] - 1)`, with labels using `len(index_names) - 1` at `:168-169`. (3) The gallery is the complete per-category split file in source order with no dedup: `src/data_utils.py:144-147` self.image_names.extend(json.load(f)) over split.{dress_type}.{split}.json; classic-mode dataset built at `src/validate.py:127`, features extracted at `:128`, iterated with shuffle=False. metric_provenance.source_excerpt_or_description: §4.1: 'We perform the experiments using two CLIP models of different sizes. The smallest one relies on a modified ResNet-50 (RN-50) architecture. It takes input images of 224 x 224, and the size of its embedding space is d = 1024. The biggest one, denoted as RN-50x4, follows the EfficientNet-style model scaling and uses approximately 4x the computation of RN-50. It takes input images of 288 x 288, and the size of its embedding space is d = 640.' §4.1: 'we set the batch size to 512 for fine-tuning the RN-50-based CLIP model and 192 for fine-tuning the RN-50x4-based model ... During the training of the Combiner network ... We set the batch size to 4096 when using both backbones. We used the PyTorch library throughout the experiments. We set the target ratio in the preprocessing pipeline to 1.25.' §4.2.1: 'FashionIQ is composed of 77,684 fashion images ... Among the 46,609 training images, there are 18,000 training triplets ... The validation and test sets consist of 15,537 and 15,538 images, respectively, with 6,017 and 6,119 triplets.'
